presentation.name: Structure Airflow DAGs for safe, cheap imports
presentation.summary: Structures Airflow DAGs so nothing expensive or fragile runs at import time.
benefits: Keeps connections and queries out of module scope, where the scheduler re-runs them
Applies consistent default_args, retries and scheduling across DAGs
Flags import-time work that makes the scheduler slow or unstable

presentation.name: Review a code change for correctness and risk
presentation.summary: Reviews a code change for correctness, risk, test coverage and backward compatibility.
benefits: Establishes what the change is supposed to do before judging whether it does it
Separates blocking defects from preferences, so findings are actionable
Checks backward compatibility for callers the diff does not show
Reports unverified areas instead of implying the whole change was checked
Accounts for every file in the diff, so a skipped file cannot pass as a reviewed one
Re-checks findings before reporting and drops only those the code disproves

presentation.name: Write code comments in the right place and keep them true
presentation.summary: Decides what a code comment says and where it goes, and keeps comments true as the code changes.
benefits: Puts each check's comment directly above it, with a failure case traced against the code
Keeps design arguments, history and runbooks out of the code and in the docs
Lists the columns a helper generates in every model that uses it
Updates or removes comments when the code they describe changes
Covers dbt and Dataform: schema.yml versus SQL comments, Jinja inside comments, pre_operations

presentation.name: Check work does what was asked before reporting done
presentation.summary: Checks that work actually does what was asked before it is reported as finished.
benefits: Requires observed command output before any claim that something passes
Separates passed, failed, skipped and never-run instead of merging them
Checks the original request was met, not only that the code runs
Reports what was not verified rather than leaving it implied

presentation.name: Trace wrong data when the pipeline succeeded
presentation.summary: Traces wrong data back to the code that produced it when the pipeline reported success.
benefits: Keeps the investigation read-only until a cause is proven
Turns symptoms into hypotheses a single query can rule out
Records evidence and unproven gaps in a written incident log

presentation.name: Diagnose a failing dbt build from compiled SQL

Says when to stop patching symptoms and fix the source

presentation.name: Trace a dbt column upstream and downstream
presentation.summary: Traces where a dbt model's column came from and what depends on it, without reading SQL by hand across the model chain.
benefits: Answers 'where did this field come from' and 'what breaks if I change it' from the dbt Cloud Discovery API
Shows the transformation type at each hop (passthrough, transformed, renamed), not just the model names
Validates model and column names before tracing, so a typo returns an error instead of a silent empty result

Handles late-arriving rows instead of silently dropping them
Detects divergence between incremental and full-refresh output

presentation.name: Define what belongs in each dbt layer
presentation.summary: Establishes what belongs in each dbt layer and why the boundaries hold.
benefits: Places sources, staging, intermediate and mart logic consistently
Applies contracts and tests at the layer where they are meaningful
Prevents business logic leaking into the staging layer

Builds the staging layer before porting business logic
Reconciles migrated output against the legacy result

benefits: Reads the project's existing layering and naming before writing
Builds and inspects real output rather than only compiling
Checks grain and row counts before the model is called done

presentation.name: Write dbt model and column descriptions
presentation.summary: Writes model and column descriptions that state what the SQL cannot.
benefits: Puts the model's grain first, so consumers know what a row is
Records business rules, units and timezones that are invisible in the data
Skips filler descriptions that only restate the column name

presentation.name: Refactor a dbt model and prove output is unchanged
presentation.summary: Restructures a dbt model while proving its output did not change.
benefits: Finds the full downstream blast radius from the dbt graph, not grep
Captures the current output before any edit
Separates safe internal changes from interface changes that break consumers

presentation.name: Pick dbt schema tests for each column role
presentation.summary: Picks dbt schema tests that catch real defects for each column role.
benefits: Chooses tests by what the column is, not by habit
Covers keys, relationships and accepted values where they matter
Gives a procedure for what to do when a test fails

presentation.name: Wire a local data stack in Compose with real readiness checks
presentation.summary: Wires local data stacks in Compose so services wait for a database to be ready, not merely started.
benefits: Waits on health checks and completed init jobs instead of container start
Keeps database data in named volumes and secrets out of the committed file
Publishes datastore ports to loopback only
Separates development overrides from the base file

presentation.name: Confirm data loss before Docker cleanup commands run
presentation.summary: Stops Docker cleanup commands from deleting data until the loss has been stated and confirmed.
benefits: Names exactly what a prune, force-remove or volume delete would take before running it
Offers a narrower command when the real problem is disk space or a stuck container
Tells the user which volumes a command does and does not touch
Lets a single stopped test container be removed without needless confirmation

presentation.name: Build Python data images that cache well and keep secrets out
presentation.summary: Builds Python data images that keep credentials out of layers, cache well and run as non-root.
benefits: Supplies pip, dbt and Git credentials through build secrets so they never land in an image layer
Orders the Dockerfile so dependency installs are cached across code changes
Separates build tools from the runtime image and runs the process as a non-root user
Checks image metadata and all layer contents for credentials, including deleted files

presentation.name: Add a first Docker setup to a Python data project
presentation.summary: Adds a first working Docker setup to a Python data project, with its dependencies as Compose services.
benefits: Creates .dockerignore, Dockerfile and compose.yaml together so the first build is clean
Runs databases and brokers as pinned containers instead of host installs
Defaults to loopback ports and a documented development-only credential
Confirms the stack actually starts before calling the scaffold done

presentation.name: Prove the cause of a code failure before fixing it
presentation.summary: Finds the cause of a failure by narrowing it down and proving it before changing code.
benefits: Establishes a reliable reproduction before theorising about causes
Turns guesses into hypotheses that a single observation can rule out
Confirms the cause explains every symptom, not just the loudest one
Stops speculative edits that hide a defect instead of fixing it

presentation.name: Split a monolithic ETL function into testable units
presentation.summary: Splits a monolithic extract-transform-load function into testable units with I/O at the edges.
benefits: Isolates the transform so it can be tested without network or database
Puts fetch and write behind thin I/O modules
Says when a function is small enough to leave alone

presentation.name: Turn agreed requirements into a step-by-step plan
presentation.summary: Turns agreed requirements into an ordered plan with verifiable steps.
benefits: Breaks work into steps that can each be checked independently
Orders steps so the riskiest assumption is tested early
States done criteria per step, not just for the whole task
Names what the plan does not cover, instead of implying full scope

presentation.name: Generate SQL from natural language, validated before it runs
presentation.summary: Generates SQL from natural language without letting an unvalidated query reach the database.
benefits: Rejects writes, unlisted tables, and multi-statement SQL with an independent validator instead of a prompt instruction
Surfaces ambiguous business-term-to-column mappings instead of silently guessing
Bounds execution with a read-only identity, statement timeout, and result limits
Returns SQL, assumptions, and a validation trace so a result can be audited, not just trusted

presentation.name: Pick the cheapest checks a pipeline change needs
presentation.summary: Selects the cheapest checks that would actually catch the regression a change can cause.
benefits: Maps the type of change to the layers of testing it requires
Avoids full end-to-end runs for defects a unit test would catch
Records which layers were skipped rather than implying full coverage

presentation.name: Review the data a pipeline run actually produced
presentation.summary: Reviews the data a pipeline run actually produced, not just whether tests passed.
benefits: Reconciles row accounting so silently dropped rows surface
Checks keys, contracts and drift against a recorded baseline
Reports INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE instead of guessing a verdict

presentation.name: Execute a plan step by step and handle divergence
presentation.summary: Works through an agreed plan one step at a time and handles it when reality diverges.
benefits: Keeps each step small enough to verify before the next one starts
Gives a rule for when to adapt the plan and when to stop and ask
Prevents unrequested scope from being added mid-execution
Keeps the plan and the actual state of the work in agreement

presentation.name: Adapt installed skills to this repository
presentation.summary: Adapts installed toolset skills by adding repository paths, commands, conventions and examples inside each installed SKILL.md.
benefits: Gives each installed skill the project paths and commands it needs
Binds generic terminology and examples to actual repository conventions
Shows proposed adaptations and asks only about material ambiguity
Preserves generic instructions and refreshes a separate project context section
Keeps context inside the installed skills without changing agent rules files

presentation.name: Document decisions and boundaries code can't show
presentation.summary: Documents architecture decisions, component boundaries and constraints a reader cannot infer from the code.
benefits: Records why a decision was made, not just what the code does
Makes component boundaries and their contracts explicit
Captures non-obvious constraints before they are rediscovered the hard way
Keeps documentation updated in the same change that invalidates it

presentation.name: Test pipeline code with pytest, mocking I/O
presentation.summary: Tests data pipeline code with pytest, mocking at the I/O boundary.
benefits: Draws a clear unit and integration split for pipeline code
Mocks at the I/O edge so transforms stay genuinely tested
Adds DAG import tests that catch breakage before deployment

presentation.name: Plan a refactor in behaviour-preserving steps
presentation.summary: Plans and sequences a refactor so behaviour is provably unchanged at every step.
benefits: Establishes a behavioural baseline before the first edit
Separates internal restructuring from interface changes that break callers
Sequences the work so each step can be verified and reverted alone
Says when a refactor should stop rather than expand

presentation.name: Work out what is needed before writing code
presentation.summary: Works out what is actually needed before any code is written.
benefits: Surfaces the real goal behind a requested solution
Separates stated requirements from assumptions that were never confirmed
Makes constraints and non-goals explicit before design starts
Says when enough is known to begin, so discovery does not run forever

presentation.name: Implement SCD Type 2 with correct validity intervals
presentation.summary: Implements Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 in SQL with correct validity intervals.
benefits: Builds non-overlapping validity intervals with exactly one current row
Detects real attribute changes instead of rewriting history on every load
Avoids the idempotency traps that duplicate rows on re-run

presentation.name: Decide what personal data a model may carry
presentation.summary: Decides what personal data a model may carry, and keeps deletion possible later.
benefits: Classifies columns by how they identify someone, including the combinations that do
Tokenises identifiers so joins survive and identity does not
Keeps personal data out of logs, lower environments and test fixtures
Designs history so an erasure request does not break the dimension

presentation.name: Find Snowflake queries worth optimising
presentation.summary: Finds the Snowflake queries actually worth optimising and reads the metrics that point at a fix.
benefits: Picks the right history view for the question being asked
Ranks by credits rather than elapsed time when cost is the concern
Turns query metrics into a specific next action

presentation.name: Restore grants after Snowflake objects are recreated
presentation.summary: Restores access after Snowflake objects are recreated, without guessing at roles.
benefits: Diffs the grants that should exist against the grants in place and emits the GRANTs to close the gap
Catches access that was lost because ownership moved, which COPY GRANTS does not carry over
Reports every grant it could not establish instead of inventing a role for it
Verifies access under the consumer role itself, with secondary roles off

access: A Snowflake connection the agent can run SQL through
A role that can see the query in query history and read its profile

presentation.name: Diagnose one Snowflake query from its profile
presentation.summary: Diagnoses one Snowflake query from its profile and operator statistics.
benefits: Reads pruning and spill statistics to locate the real bottleneck
Separates a query problem from a warehouse sizing problem
Points at the specific operator responsible for the cost

presentation.name: Rewrite Snowflake SQL without changing results
presentation.summary: Rewrites a Snowflake query for performance without changing its results.
benefits: Separates transformations that are safe from ones that only look safe
Explains why each rewrite preserves the result set
Keeps null and duplicate semantics intact through the rewrite

access: A Snowflake connection the agent can run SQL through
A read role with USAGE on the warehouse, databases and schemas, SELECT on the base tables and the semantic view, and the SNOWFLAKE.GOVERNANCE_VIEWER database role

presentation.name: Repair Snowflake semantic view drift
presentation.summary: Finds where a semantic view no longer matches its tables and repairs it without losing hand-written descriptions.
benefits: Classifies drift as added, dropped, renamed or retyped columns, since each needs a different fix
Keeps a renamed column's element name and description instead of replacing them with a new element
Carries existing comments, synonyms and instructions into the regenerated view
Flags new columns that need a description instead of inventing one

presentation.name: Edit technical prose without changing meaning
presentation.summary: Improves technical prose without changing its meaning or terminology.
benefits: Removes padding and boilerplate that add length but no information
Preserves defined terms and technical claims exactly as written
Replaces unnatural phrasing with how an engineer would actually say it
Flags sentences whose meaning is unclear instead of guessing at them

tools: Terraform CLI, or Terragrunt, to produce the JSON plan
access: Provider credentials for the target environment, when the plan has to be made rather than an existing one reviewed

presentation.name: Review a Terraform plan in plain language before apply
presentation.summary: Reads a Terraform plan before it is applied and restates each change in plain language, so a reviewer without deep Terraform knowledge can approve or stop it.
benefits: Lists every destroy and replacement with the reason Terraform recorded for it
Flags changes that lose data or identity, and in-place updates that are not harmless
Checks IAM, trust and bucket policy changes on AWS for wildcards and wrong ARNs
Catches Terragrunt inputs that are silently dropped and plans built on mock outputs
Summarises a plan with a script that never prints secret values and fails on destroys

presentation.name: Replicate Terragrunt units across tenants without drift
presentation.summary: Adds or moves Terragrunt units in bulk and verifies every tenant and environment got the intended copy.
benefits: Picks the template unit by comparing every existing instance
Catches values copied from the wrong tenant, missing units and shared state keys
Diffs units across tenants with a bundled read-only script
Keeps state migration a separate, confirmed step when a service moves

presentation.name: Decide what to test and whether tests catch defects
presentation.summary: Decides what is worth testing and judges whether existing tests would catch a defect.
benefits: Derives cases from behaviour and boundaries rather than from code shape
Identifies tests that pass regardless of whether the code is correct
Covers failure paths, not only the successful one
Distinguishes untested code from code that cannot be tested as written
